title: Analysing running time and space
lead: An Essential section on the model of computation, on measuring running time and space by counting, and on the three kinds of running-time guarantee. Erickson’s Running Time passage returns to BottlesOfBeer, peasant multiplication, ApportionCongress and lattice multiplication from 1.1; his pseudocode counts from 1 (for i ← 1 to n, gifts[2 .. n]), while the Python, Java, C++ and JavaScript translations count from 0.
notes: Erickson’s chapter 0 exercises, with his Figure 0.6, and the last paragraph of ODS’s model of computation, which its pseudocode edition prints cut short, are left out here.
exercise_notes: The OpenDSA items the chapter config lists for this section (AnlsIntroMCQszip with FasterCorASumm, tagged with need-for-efficiency too; MthBgMCQrmacc and MthBgMCQdskacc; AnalProgramMCQtheta1–9 with AnalProgramSumm; AnalProblemTF1, TF2 and TF4–TF7 with AnalProblemSumm; AlgAnlsMCQsqlsrch, AlgAnlsTFsqlsrch1 and AlgAnlsTFsqlsrch2; MisunderstandingsTF1–6 with MisSumm, tagged with big-o and big-omega-theta too) wait for the converter of OpenDSA’s Khan-format exercises and are not here yet. Erickson’s chapter 0 exercises 1, 2 and 3 (songs of other running times, singing time counted in syllables, and The Barley Mow with his Figure 0.6) and Applied Combinatorics’ basics exercises have no published answers and are left out. OpenDSA AnalProblemTF10–12, which assume sorting, are held for chapter 10, MIT 6.006 S20 ps0 0-6 for 2.3 and MIT 6.006 F11 ps1 1-3 to 1-6 for chapter 6.

The inequality undercounts the work of one step. A step of the recursion makes a parity test, a mediation ⌊x/2⌋, a duplation y + y and, when x is odd, one more addition + y: up to four of the operations T counts, so it should read T(x, y) ≤ T(⌊x/2⌋, 2y) + 4. The bound T(x, y) = O(log x) is unchanged.

Here the Census Bureau’s priority queue is an unsorted array; in Erickson’s Congressional Apportionment (Section 1.1) the Bureau uses a sorted array, stored in a single column of an Excel spreadsheet and recalculated from scratch at every iteration. With the unsorted array, ExtractMax scans all n states and the O(Rn) bound follows as stated; recalculating the sorted column for every seat takes Ω(n) time a seat as well, so either way the Bureau’s implementation takes Ω(Rn) time.
